title: Potential and limits of intensive care medicine: Prevalence, causes and possible solutions to ethical challenges in German intensive care units - the intensivist’s view
summary:
Modern medicine allows nowadays effective treatment of patients with even the most severe acute illnesses through intensive care interventions. However, the wide range of possibilities offered by modern intensive care medicine also raises questions about its limitations and the appropriate provision of treatment. Intensive care physicians regularly encounter ethically challenging situations in their clinical practice. One particular challenge is to develop individually tailored treatment strategies that take into account available medical options, the acute clinical condition and pre-existing comorbidities, the patient's prognosis, as well as their treatment goals and overall well-being. Patients with a poor prognosis or severe pre-existing conditions may receive invasive treatments that may be associated with considerable physical and psychological burdens, while a more appropriate palliative approach may not be sufficiently considered. Healthcare professionals may experience ethical conflicts and emotional distress when they consider a patient's treatment as potentially inappropriate in view of their individual goals or overall well-being.

The issue of potentially inappropriate care in intensive care units has attracted considerable attention internationally over the past several years. The present study protocol describes the first survey of its kind to be conducted in intensive care units in Germany. Its primary aim is to assess how frequently intensivists perceive treatment as potentially inappropriate and to identify the factors contributing to these perceptions.
Physicians' perceptions will be investigated using a structured questionnaire. In addition to the reasons underlying the perception of potentially inappropriate care, the study will collect patient-related factors, reasons for initiating or continuing intensive care interventions, and potential strategies for addressing such situations.
conditions: Potentially inappropriate care as assessed by intensive care physicians

interventions.name:
On the day of data collection, the senior physicians in charge of the German ICU participating in the study will be surveyed using an online questionnaire regarding their individual assessment of the treatment of all patients currently treated on their respective ICU.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Intensive care unit (ICU) lead physician of a German ICU

Assessment of clinical patient cases (anonymized):
Patients aged ≥18 years who are treated on the ICU on the day of observation
Exclusion criteria:
Non-physician ICU staff, Physicians in postgraduate training, Physicians other than the ICU lead physician, staff from other hospital departments

Exclusion criteria for patient cases:
Patients aged under 18 years; Patients admitted to intermediate care units or other non-ICU hospital wards
